title: Pinned gluing across a finite modification
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $n\geq1$, and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. Let $X$ be Noetherian excellent with $\ell$ invertible and dimension function $\delta$ [def-exc-excellent-ring, def-per-potential-dualizing-complex]. Let $i:Y\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion with complementary open $U$, and $p:X'\to X$ a finite morphism inducing an isomorphism $p^{-1}U\to U$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Form $Y'=Y\times_XX'$ with maps $i':Y'\to X'$, $p':Y'\to Y$, and $q=pi'=ip'$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Give $X',Y,Y'$ their induced dimension functions $\delta_W(w)=\delta(f(w))$. Suppose each of these three schemes admits a pinned potential dualizing complex, any two on each scheme have a unique pinning-preserving isomorphism, and for every such complex $L$ on each scheme $W$ the scalar map $\Lambda_W\to\tau_{\leq0}R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(L,L)$ is an isomorphism [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Then these three assertions hold on $X$ as well. More precisely, writing $K_{X'},K_Y,K_{Y'}$ for the chosen pinned complexes, the adjunction maps from $K_{Y'}\cong p'^!K_Y\cong i'^!K_{X'}$ give a distinguished triangle
$$q_*K_{Y'}\xrightarrow{(+,-)}i_*K_Y\oplus p_*K_{X'}\longrightarrow K_X\longrightarrow q_*K_{Y'}[1]$$
in $D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Its cone admits pinnings for which $K_Y\to i^!K_X$ and $K_{X'}\to p^!K_X$ are pinning-preserving isomorphisms. Here for a finite map $f$, $f^!$ is the bounded-below right adjoint to $f_*=Rf_!$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support].

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 5.4.1 and its proof, pp. 290-293 (existence, pinned comparison, and scalar Hom rigidity; no perversity clause is asserted here)

proof.text:
For any finite map $f$ in the square, finite direct image is exact by [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact], also for $\Lambda$-modules since exactness is detected on underlying abelian sheaves. Check the constant-sheaf sequence
$$0\longrightarrow\Lambda_X\xrightarrow{(+,+)}i_*\Lambda_Y\oplus p_*\Lambda_{X'}\xrightarrow{(+,-)}q_*\Lambda_{Y'}\longrightarrow0.$$
At a geometric point $x\notin Y$, [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula] gives $0\to\Lambda\xrightarrow{1}\Lambda\to0$. At $x\in Y$, let $E$ be the finite geometric fibre of $p$. The sequence is $0\to\Lambda\to\Lambda\oplus\Lambda^E\to\Lambda^E\to0$, with $a\mapsto(a,(a)_e)$ and $(b,(c_e))\mapsto(b-c_e)_e$. The last map is onto, by taking $b=0,c_e=-d_e$, and its kernel is exactly the diagonal. This remains valid for $E=\varnothing$. Exactness of stalks and their conservativity [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact, lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] give the asserted sheaf sequence.

source.place: XVII, proof of Proposition 5.4.1, p. 291, initial constant-sheaf exact sequence

proof.text: Every finite map here is compactifiable using itself as the proper part and the identity as open part. Finite-type affine algebras over excellent rings are excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent]; thus the schemes in the square meet the hypotheses of [lem-per-potential-dualizing-finite-pullback]. That result makes $p'^!K_Y$ and $i'^!K_{X'}$ potential for the induced dimension function (the residue transcendence degrees are zero). By the assumed pinned uniqueness on $Y'$, choose their unique pinned identifications with $K_{Y'}$. Adjunction gives $a:q_*K_{Y'}\to i_*K_Y$ and $b:q_*K_{Y'}\to p_*K_{X'}$. Complete $(a,-b)$ to a distinguished triangle and call its third object $K_X$. Exact finite direct image and closure of $D^+$ under finite cones ensure $K_X\in D^+$. Denote the two maps to $K_X$ by $u:i_*K_Y\to K_X$ and $v:p_*K_{X'}\to K_X$. The triangle relation is $ua=vb$.

source.place: XVII, proof of Proposition 5.4.1, p. 291, construction by the difference of the counits

proof.text: Write $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, $j':U\hookrightarrow X'$ using the given isomorphism. Restrict the defining triangle to $U$. The two terms supported on $Y$ disappear and $j^*p_*K_{X'}=j'^*K_{X'}$: at every geometric point the finite-stalk formula gives precisely its unique fibre factor. Thus $j^*v$ is an isomorphism. By open restriction, [lem-per-potential-dualizing-finite-pullback] makes this restricted complex potential. Transfer its pinnings on each residue-field etale site to $K_X$ at points of $U$, using the costalk convention of [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex]; their geometric fibres are taken afterwards.

source.place: XVII, proof of Proposition 5.4.1, p. 291, paragraph restricting to U

proof.text: Apply $i^!$ to the triangle. The exchange and its counit normalization in [lem-per-finite-closed-support-exchange] make $i^!b$ an isomorphism. Moreover $i^!i_*K_Y=K_Y$: exact fully faithful closed pushforward [prop-openclosed-lowerstar-fully-faithful] remains fully faithful on derived categories (apply the exact $i^*$ to its degreewise counit), so the unit of its right adjunction is invertible. The first arrow of the resulting triangle has the form $(c,-1):D\to K_Y\oplus D$. The automorphism $(y,d)\mapsto(y+cd,d)$ changes it to $(0,-1)$; hence its cone is $K_Y$, with the map from the first summand an isomorphism. Consequently the adjoint $u^\flat:K_Y\to i^!K_X$ is an isomorphism. For each $y\in Y$, the closed-immersion costalk identification of [lem-per-exceptional-costalk-gysin] gives $C_yK_Y\cong C_{i(y)}K_X$ on the residue-field etale site. Transport $p_y$ through its inverse to obtain the residue-field pinning of [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex], and then take its geometric fibres. Together with Step 3 these make $K_X$ pointwise pinned, with no residue compatibility across the boundary yet claimed.

source.place: XVII, proof of Proposition 5.4.1, p. 291, i!-comparison and putative pinnings

proof.text:
Let $v^\flat:K_{X'}\to p^!K_X$ be adjoint to $v$. Transpose $ua=vb$ through the composite adjunctions. It says that the following two maps from $K_{Y'}$ to $q^!K_X$ are equal:
$$K_{Y'}\cong p'^!K_Y\xrightarrow{p'^!u^\flat}p'^!i^!K_X\cong q^!K_X,$$
$$K_{Y'}\cong i'^!K_{X'}\xrightarrow{i'^!v^\flat}i'^!p^!K_X\cong q^!K_X.$$
Transitivity of the costalk comparisons [lem-per-exceptional-costalk-gysin] identifies the induced pointwise pinnings under these composition maps, even for the pointwise pinned $K_X$. The first line is an isomorphism preserving those pinnings by Step 4, so $i'^!v^\flat$ is an isomorphism preserving them as well. Over $U$, source locality of the exceptional adjoint [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality] identifies $j'^*p^!K_X$ with $j^*K_X$; under this identification $j'^*v^\flat=j^*v$, an isomorphism preserving the pinnings of Step 3. The localization triangle [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle] applied to a cone of $v^\flat$ shows that a morphism killed by both $i'^!$ and $j'^*$ is an isomorphism. Therefore $v^\flat$ is a pinning-preserving isomorphism on $X'$.

source.place: XVII, proof of Proposition 5.4.1, p. 292, equality of the two adjoints and comparison on X′

proof.text: The finite map $r:X'\sqcup Y\to X$ with components $p,i$ is surjective: $p$ covers $U$, and $i$ covers $Y$. Its exceptional pullback is the pair $(p^!K_X,i^!K_X)$, since finite disjoint-union sheaves, direct images and Hom adjunctions are componentwise. Steps 4 and 5 identify these, with their induced pinnings, with $K_{X'}$ and $K_Y$. They are potential by hypothesis. Apply [lem-per-finite-surjective-potential-detection] to $r$ and the pointwise pinned $K_X$ to conclude the exact compatibility required by [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex]: $p_{\bar y}=p_{\bar x}(1)[2]\circ\operatorname{sp}_{\bar y,\bar x}$ at every immediate geometric specialization, with its fixed normalized transition $d^{-1}\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde Z}(\nu^*i^!(K_X|_{X_{(\bar x)}}))$. This is the transition after strict localization, with the signed twist/shift identification prescribed there. Thus $K_X$ is potential. The use of $r$ is necessary because the hypotheses do not say that $p$ is surjective. This proves existence and both asserted pinned comparisons.

source.place: XVII, Proposition 2.4.3.3 and proof of Proposition 5.4.1, pp. 291-292: use the covering finite family {p,i}

proof.text:
For any potential complex $K$ on $X$, turn the sheaf sequence of Step 1 into a triangle using [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle]. Apply $R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(-,K)$, which carries triangles to triangles [lem-sf-hom-triangulated]. The finite internal-Hom adjunction [lem-per-finite-exceptional-internal-hom], including its counit normalization, identifies the resulting triangle as
$$q_*q^!K\xrightarrow{(+,-)}i_*i^!K\oplus p_*p^!K\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow q_*q^!K[1].$$
Here $R\mathcal Hom(\Lambda_X,K)=K$, as is immediate from the Hom-complex model with the coefficient unit as first variable. The pullback result [lem-per-potential-dualizing-finite-pullback] makes the three extraordinary restrictions potential. Their unique pinned identifications with the chosen complexes identify the first arrow with $(a,-b)$ of Step 2. This gives the canonical triangle once a pinned potential complex is fixed, without assuming that arbitrary triangulated cones are canonically chosen.

source.place: XVII, proof of Proposition 5.4.1, p. 291, first paragraph: dualizing the constant sequence

proof.text:
Let $K,L$ be any two potential complexes on $X$. By [lem-per-potential-dualizing-finite-pullback], their restrictions $f^!K,f^!L$ are potential for $f=i,p,q$. The assumed uniqueness on $Y,X',Y'$ gives isomorphisms $\alpha_f:f^!K\to f^!L$. Their induced maps on $q^!K$ agree, since composition preserves pinnings and there is only one pinned isomorphism on $Y'$. Composing $\alpha_f$ with scalar endomorphisms, the assumed scalar rigidity on the three schemes identifies
$$\tau_{\leq0}R\mathcal Hom(f^!K,f^!L)\cong\Lambda_{\operatorname{dom}(f)}.$$
Apply $R\mathcal Hom(-,L)$ to Step 7 and use [lem-sf-hom-triangulated, lem-per-finite-exceptional-internal-hom]. The result is a triangle
$$H\longrightarrow B\xrightarrow{d} C\longrightarrow H[1],$$
where $H=R\mathcal Hom(K,L)$, $B=i_*R\mathcal Hom(i^!K,i^!L)\oplus p_*R\mathcal Hom(p^!K,p^!L)$ and $C=q_*R\mathcal Hom(q^!K,q^!L)$. The counit compatibility of the internal-Hom adjunction identifies $H^0(d)$ with $(b,(c_e))\mapsto(b-c_e)_e$, or sheafwise $(+,-)$ on $i_*\Lambda\oplus p_*\Lambda\to q_*\Lambda$. This follows because each restriction takes $\alpha_i$ or $\alpha_p$ to the same $\alpha_q$, and is linear on scalars.

source.place: XVII, proof of Proposition 5.4.1, pp. 292-293, compatible pinned isomorphisms and internal-Hom triangle

proof.text:
Exact finite pushforward [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact] and the assumed scalar rigidity imply $H^r(B)=H^r(C)=0$ for $r<0$. The cohomology sequence of Step 8 then gives $H^r(H)=0$ for $r<0$ and
$$H^0(H)=\ker\bigl(i_*\Lambda_Y\oplus p_*\Lambda_{X'}\xrightarrow{(+,-)}q_*\Lambda_{Y'}\bigr)=\Lambda_X,$$
with the last equality proved in Step 1. Hence $\tau_{\leq0}H\cong\Lambda_X$. The diagonal section $1$ gives a map $\Lambda_X\to\tau_{\leq0}H\to H$, hence a morphism $\psi:K\to L$ by [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections]. Its exceptional restrictions are $\alpha_i,\alpha_p$, by the counit-normalized comparisons in Step 8. In particular it preserves all pointwise pinnings. It is invertible: it is an isomorphism after $i^!$, and also on $U$ since $p$ is an isomorphism there; the localization triangle [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle] kills its cone.

source.place: XVII, proof of Proposition 5.4.1, p. 293, low-degree cohomology and the distinguished global morphism

proof.text: Because $H=R\mathcal Hom(K,L)$ has no negative cohomology, degree-zero hypercohomology equals $\Gamma(X,H^0(H))$: in a bounded-below representative beginning in degree zero, both groups are the kernel of $\Gamma(H^0\text{-term})\to\Gamma(H^1\text{-term})$, since sections preserve kernels. Thus [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] identifies all morphisms $K\to L$ with $\Gamma(X,\Lambda_X)$, taking a scalar $\lambda$ to $\lambda\psi$. A pinning-preserving isomorphism has scalar $1$ at every point (its map on the rank-one costalk is the identity), hence $\lambda=1$ by stalk conservativity. This proves unique pinned isomorphism. For $K=L$, the normalized local isomorphisms are the identities, and Step 9's isomorphism $\Lambda_X\to\tau_{\leq0}R\mathcal Hom(K,K)$ is exactly scalar action, since its two restrictions send $1$ to the identities. This proves the scalar-rigidity clause for every potential complex on $X$.

source.place: XVII, proof of Proposition 5.4.1, pp. 292-293, uniqueness with fixed pinnings and scalar normalization
